text: I see so the problem is then if it lives there i press play now i have no way home. shitty idea just put the whole chrome in the bag bro
resolution: Collapsed the three misaligned chrome axes into one row and made the chrome persist across both routes. Root cause: the Editor/Play toggle was an absolutely-positioned floating overlay rendered at the router level (sibling of the routes), parked in a hardcoded paddingRight:150 gap on the chrome bar — it only approximately aligned with the brand/menus/Compile that live in the real flex row, and it floated at router level precisely so it survived the /play route. Simply folding it into Chrome would have stranded /play with no way home. Fix: AppFrame is now the persistent shell for BOTH routes — it mounts once directly under <Router> (index.tsx no longer swaps AppFrame vs PlayRoute via <Route>), reads useRoute(), and swaps only its body (editor panels on /editor, host-native WorldLoader/PlayRoute on /play). The top chrome is always mounted, so /play keeps the Editor/Play toggle and editor state survives the round trip. RouteToggle lost position:absolute and became a real inline member of the chrome row (Chrome.tsx, after Compile), sharing the bar's single alignItems:center centerline; removed the paddingRight:150 reservation. Files: index.tsx, shell/AppFrame.tsx, shell/Chrome.tsx, RouteToggle.tsx, editor.cls.ts (ED_RouteToggle inline), workspace.cls.ts (HW_Chrome padding + HW_PlayBody). Verified all four TSX parse clean via esbuild transform; did not ship (live session).
